author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: The veterinarian list can be narrowed to one specialty
summary: Both veterinarian list surfaces (the paged HTML directory at /vets.html and the machine-readable list at /vets) accept an optional specialty query parameter that narrows the list to veterinarians holding that specialty. The filter is a URL contract only; no page control is added.
acceptance_criteria: [REQ-VET-003] GET /vets.html?specialty=<name> shows only the veterinarians holding that specialty; paging (page count and page contents) applies to the narrowed list.
[REQ-VET-003] GET /vets?specialty=<name> returns only the veterinarians holding that specialty in the machine-readable list.
[REQ-VET-003] Matching is on the whole specialty name, disregarding letter case: 'RADIOLOGY' matches radiology; a prefix such as 'radio' matches no veterinarian.
[REQ-VET-003] A specialty held by no veterinarian, or not on the clinic's list at all, yields HTTP 200 with the usual page or JSON document and an empty veterinarian list.
[REQ-VET-003] An empty or whitespace-only specialty value produces the same result on both surfaces as a request without the parameter.
[REQ-VET-003] On a narrowed HTML directory, every pagination link (numbered, first, previous, next, last) carries the same specialty parameter, so following it keeps the narrowing.
[REQ-VET-003] A listed veterinarian holding the named specialty among others is shown with every specialty they hold, not only the named one.
[REQ-VET-001] [REQ-VET-004] Without the parameter, both surfaces behave exactly as today: the paged HTML directory and the full machine-readable list with each veterinarian's specialties.
non_goals: Free-text search over veterinarian names or any attribute the directory does not show (NG-9, narrowed)
A form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing a specialty on either surface (owner-deferred to a follow-up request)
Narrowing by more than one specialty in one request (open question in the PRD)
New user-facing wording, such as a heading naming the active specialty or a no-matches message (open question in the PRD)
Any behavior promise for a specialty value with surrounding spaces (open question in the PRD; tests pin neither reading)
notes: Two requirement IDs: REQ-VET-003 is the specialty filter; REQ-VET-004 is minted per intake decision 2 for the reinstated machine-readable surface (/vets), whose base behavior already exists and is covered by the existing showResourcesVetList test. REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn in the Superseded list. The slice's commit should name both REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004 so the backlog reads both as delivered. Design follow-ups outside this expert's write scope: docs/system-design.md still says the machine-readable route serves no requirement (Contracts table row for Vets/VetController and the known-issues row) and should map it to REQ-VET-004 and record the specialty parameter; docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for docs/adr/2026-09-29-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md. Seed data has at most two veterinarians per specialty against a page size of five, so the paging acceptance needs a fixture with more matches than one page.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Existing vet feature package, extended in place, with no new module or pattern. The narrowing follows the owner-search seam: a Spring Data derived query with a Pageable, backing OwnerRepository and OwnerController (grep, the weaker basis; IDE oracle not connected). Adjustments: one uncached repository query shared by both routes; an optional specialty request parameter on GET /vets.html and GET /vets; pagination links that carry the parameter. system-design.md now maps REQ-VET-003/REQ-VET-004 on the Vet, Specialty, Vets, VetRepository, VetController and CacheConfiguration rows. It also gains a Contracts invariant for the narrowing, a new § Scale and Load section, and three Threat Model rows, and drops the 'machine-readable route serves no requirement' Known Defects row, since REQ-VET-004 reinstates the route. REQ-VET-004's base behavior is already implemented and covered by showResourcesVetList. No ADR: no decision here constrains later slices beyond the recorded current state. The NG-9 narrowing is already recorded in the non-goal ADR.
integration_points: Binding, GET /vets.html: a new optional request-scoped String request parameter `specialty` beside the existing int `page`. No persisted type is bound. Normalization is web-controller binding (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row): a null, empty or whitespace-only value selects the existing unnarrowed read, and any other value passes to the repository unmodified.

Binding, GET /vets: the same optional request-scoped String `specialty` parameter with the same normalization. A narrowed request wraps the narrowed query's full result in the existing Vets wrapper. Call the query with Pageable.unpaged(), or add a List-returning sibling; the machine-readable list stays unpaged. An unnarrowed request keeps the cached findAll() call byte-for-byte.

Repository boundary: VetRepository gains one derived query, e.g. findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable) returning Page<Vet>. Equality on the upper-cased name, not StartingWith/Containing/Like; Distinct so the join cannot duplicate a veterinarian or skew the count query. No @Cacheable on it. Existing methods and their @Cacheable stay untouched. Double: the real VetRepository against the embedded H2 seed data, with no stub. Seed facts: radiology is held by Helen Leary and Henry Stevens; surgery by Linda Douglas and Rafael Ortega; dentistry by Linda Douglas only.

Paging fixture: the narrowed-paging test needs more matches than the page size (5). Insert extra veterinarians holding one specialty inside a test-managed transaction (@Transactional test plus @Sql, or the EntityManager) so they roll back. The fixture test issues only narrowed requests: an unnarrowed read in that transaction would load the fixture into the shared, uncleared vet cache.

Framework transport: MockMvc (the sanctioned transport stand-in). Put the new tests in a new VetControllerIntegrationTests (@SpringBootTest plus MockMvc, following the CrashControllerIntegrationTests naming precedent) against the real repository. Matching rules live in the query, and a stubbed repository cannot exercise them. The existing @WebMvcTest VetControllerTests and its tolerated Mockito stubs stay as-is, and no new stub is added there. All six prd-entry test names live in the new class.

Template: vetList.html receives the normalized specialty as a model attribute, absent or null when unnarrowed. Every pagination href (numbered, first, previous, next, last) carries it through Thymeleaf link-expression parameters, e.g. @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}. An unnarrowed directory renders hrefs with no specialty parameter, not even a bare 'specialty' key; guard or build the link so a null value adds nothing.

Rendering: a listed veterinarian shows every specialty they hold. The narrowing filters veterinarians in the query's where-clause, and the existing EAGER specialties mapping loads each full set. Never join-fetch the restricted collection. No new message keys and no heading change (REQ-LANG-002 untouched).

patterns.description: Derived query with Pageable returning Page: the shape the narrowed vet query follows (equality with IgnoreCase instead of StartingWith)
Request-value normalization in the controller before the repository call; the vet controller treats a blank specialty as absent
findPaginated/addPaginationModel: the narrowed directory reuses the same page size and model attributes, plus the specialty attribute

risks.risk: Narrowed directory and list paths scale with the veterinarian set (system-design.md § Scale and Load, 'Specialty-narrowed vet directory and list' row: unrecorded, treated as bounded)
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: one derived query per request, paged in the database for the directory; no in-memory filtering of the cached findAll()

risks.risk: The caller-chosen specialty keys an unbounded cache (the vet cache declares no size limit; § Scale and Load Limits line; Threat Model 'Cache growth driven by caller-chosen values' row)
risks.mitigation: No @Cacheable on the narrowed query; the vet cache keeps holding unnarrowed reads only

risks.risk: Reflected specialty in pagination hrefs turns into markup or expression injection. The existing links use __${...}__ preprocessing, and copying that pattern with a request value is template-expression injection (security-principles § Realization, Cross-site scripting and Injection rows; Threat Model 'Reflected request value in page links' row)
risks.mitigation: Link-expression parameters only. The specialty never goes inside __...__ preprocessing or string concatenation. Page-number links may keep their current form or move to parameters

risks.risk: Pattern characters in the value (% or _) widen the match, or a prefix matches (security-principles § Realization, Injection row; Threat Model 'Wildcard matching through the specialty value' row)
risks.mitigation: Equality on the case-folded whole name via the derived IgnoreCase equality, never Like/StartingWith/Containing. A test showing 'radio' matches nothing pins it

risks.risk: Case-insensitive matching diverges per vendor, as PostgreSQL owner search already does (system-design.md § Known Defects, first row)
risks.mitigation: Case folding happens in the query (upper on both sides via IgnoreCase), not in column collation, so H2, MySQL and PostgreSQL agree

risks.risk: The join duplicates veterinarians or inflates the page count (§ Scale and Load narrowed-path row: distinct veterinarians)
risks.mitigation: Distinct derived query; the paging test asserts total pages and per-page counts against the fixture

risks.risk: Unnarrowed behavior drifts, which the REQ-VET-001/REQ-VET-004 'behave exactly as today' criterion forbids: a bare 'specialty' key on hrefs, a changed repository call, or a changed cache use
risks.mitigation: Existing VetControllerTests stay green unmodified. The integration tests assert that an unnarrowed directory's hrefs carry no specialty and that a blank value matches the no-parameter result on both surfaces

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log. Open-question handling: the specialty value with surrounding spaces is pinned by no test and promised by no contract (PRD Open Questions). The design passes any non-blank value unmodified, the narrowest reading, and no test asserts either way. Unordered paging of the narrowed list mirrors today's unordered unnarrowed paging; tests assert per-page counts and membership, not cross-page order. docs/adr/README.md gains the index row for the product expert's non-goal ADR (2026-09-29-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md), as its prd-entry notes requested. Brief gap for the owner of docs/security-principles.md, outside this agent's write scope: the Realization table has no row for resource exhaustion from caller-chosen values, such as cache keys or unbounded result sets. This slice records the mitigation as a Threat Model row in system-design.md. Separately, the existing cached findAll(Pageable) is keyed by the caller-chosen page number; that predates this slice and is not in its scope. The commit should name both REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004.

findings.description: The conditional `${specialty != null} ? @{/vets.html(page=..,specialty=${specialty})} : @{/vets.html(page=..)}` is repeated verbatim across five sibling links (page numbers, first, previous, next, last). A conditional repeated across sibling sites is duplication, and a future change to the narrowing parameter must be made five times.

findings.description: `PAGE_SIZE` was widened from a method-local `int pageSize = 5` to a package-private constant. Its only non-production reader is VetControllerIntegrationTests (lines 87 and 184), so it is widened for test access, which is a placement smell.
findings.fix: Make the constant `private static final` and have the test state its own page size, so a change to the production page size fails the test visibly rather than following it silently.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the request-supplied specialty reaches the database only through the Spring Data derived query `findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String specialtyName, Pageable pageable)` (VetRepository.java diff), which binds it as a parameter. No query text is concatenated from a request value.

Cache exhaustion avoided: the new finder is deliberately left without @Cacheable. Its Javadoc reads 'Not cached: the name is chosen by the caller, and the vet cache declares no size limit', so attacker-chosen specialty strings cannot grow the unbounded `vets` cache.

Output escaping in vetList.html: the specialty value reaches the page only as a Thymeleaf link-expression parameter, `@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}`, which URL-encodes it and attribute-escapes the href. The change also removes the old `__${i}__` preprocessing from the page links. `grep -F -e utext -e '__$' vetList.html` returned no matches, so no request-derived value is preprocessed or rendered unescaped.

Blank input fails safe: `narrowingOf` maps a blank or absent specialty to null, which takes the pre-existing unfiltered path. A non-matching value returns an empty list, not an error, so no exception detail reaches the error page.

Surface: no new endpoint. Both existing GET routes (/vets.html, /vets) gain only an optional read-only request parameter. The JSON route's `Pageable.unpaged()` result is a subset of the unfiltered `findAll()` it already returned, so the response size can only shrink. No request-bound object (@ModelAttribute/@RequestBody), no logging of the value, no file, shell, or deserialization sink is added in the diff.
Test fixtures: the SQL string concatenation in VetControllerIntegrationTests uses only compile-time constants, never request input. No secrets were added anywhere in the diff.

Supply chain: build.gradle is unchanged by this slice (not in `changeset.py --name-only`). OWASP dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured (`grep -F dependencyCheck build.gradle` has no match), so no NVD match ran in this review. `./gradlew dependencies` resolves spring-boot-starter-webmvc 4.1.1, jackson-databind 3.1.5 and thymeleaf-spring6 3.1.5.RELEASE.

That finder is still not @Cacheable, so attacker-chosen names cannot grow the unbounded `vets` cache. `narrowingOf` still sends a blank value to the unfiltered path.
